reviews.comment: Wonderful prof. This is the second class I have taken with him and he has been great in explaining assignments, being available for help, and helping you to get an A in his courses. He offers a lot of extra credit, and as long as you try your best your grade will reflect that. This class also really taught me how to write a scientific paper. Easy!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is a hard class. However, it is probably my favorite lab from my undergrad. The lab reports are a bit extensive at first. Clear grading and feedback. Class seems overwhelming at first, but then is manageable. Professor super nice, an expert in his field, and enjoys teaching this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, Dr. Griffing is quite a knowledgeable professor with a chill nature. He gives A TON of extra credit and if you just put in some effort, you will actually learn some useful things if you want to work in a research lab. Slightly disorganized class, but lenient on grading and overall enjoyable. Take him if you can.
As a Spring semester senior that was very unmotivated take this class. Very chill

Took this class during COVID- it is the cell biology lab so it was a little weird having to do that online. But Dr. Griffing is great! This class was pretty intensive- weekly reports, quizzes, & discussion. At the end of the semester we designed the experiments we did, which made the class super interesting. I learned a lot about research & inquiry

Dr. Griffing was a real gem. I took him for Biological Imaging (COVID online era), so the other reviews might be reflective of another course. Dr. Griffing is VERY tech-savvy and made using image processing software very easy. The quizzes were pretty easy since they were open-book. He has many extra credit opportunities. Humorous guy. Take him!

Loved Griffing! Bio 112 is a really tough course and you are expected to study all the time no matter what. His tests were SUPER specific but all of the questions are from his lecture slides. He goes through slides REALLY fast though so just take pics of them. Had his class in the mornings and he always made my day! He is so crazy and funny

So he covers a lot but he gives you lots of chances to earn extra points (ten extra points for each of the first three exams) and via LC (I think we got the chance to earn like 45-50 extra points). He also doesn't go in order in the textbook, which can be a little confusing, but it's not a bad class. He goes through slides really fast  though.

He's a hard professor. We covered so many chapters every test but he's interesting and knows what he's talking about. You have to work for an A in this class. Doesn't post powerpoints and goes through lecture quickly so it's hard to keep up but SI really helps. He's good but hard
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He was a fairly interesting professor and knows the information he's teaching really well, but he took it upon himself to make this course into an MCAT prep-course. He covered over 20 more chapters than the other professors and there was so much information on each exam that it was extremely difficult to learn everything and do well.

Great guy but the class was very difficult. Tests were off of his powerpoints, but the amount of information you had to memorize it was overwhelming. For example, the final wasn't cumulative, but there was more stuff on it than on my cumulative chem final. Lots of easy hw. This made tests difficult. Offers some extra credit. Wouldn't take again.

honestly, if youre going to take him don't bother with buying a textbook. He reviews lectures in class, and said he makes questions by looking at the slides. Test are hard and way too detailed, they cover at least 10 chapters at a time. Homework is tedious.

Expect a lot of homework-- Mastering Biology 3x a week. Not difficult, just a lot of it. Assigned Groups in lecture to complete learning catalytics, but it wasn't that bad. His tests were straight from his lecture powerpoints, but for some reason were still challenging. He's an enthusiastic professor as well. He's not the best but not the worst.

There is no way to do all of the reading he assigns as it requires you to read a whole 30pg chapter every 2 days on top of all of the other work you have to do. You have to depend on his notes and the online material for the tests, and it's definitely not enough.

Lectures are the more boring than watching grass grow. Test are also pretty difficult. However, he posts all of his lectures online. If you can memorize those, you'll be able to do OK on the tests. Don't take him if you can help it.

We went over 1 chapter each lecture so when exams came around they were about 10 chapters long--and for the 10 chapters he went too in depth. He does give good curves, but again his exams are pretty hard that sometimes they don't help you out enough. The homework is on mastering biology and super easy.
This class was very difficult. He adds 10-15 curves on tests if necessary, but the tests are so tough that it doesn't help much.
